sections.author: M
sections.text:
**Header fields**
- Borrower: Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. [D2, header]
- Request type: Not in provided documents: the bank's formal request-type label. D2 is titled "Draft Amended and Restated Credit Agreement" [D2, header], and D5 records a request to increase the existing facility [D5, ¶4]. The underwriter should confirm the label.
- Total commitment: $18.0M: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver [D1, §3 note].
- Underwriter: Not in provided documents: assigned underwriter (internal assignment record).
- Senior reviewer: Not in provided documents: assigned senior reviewer (internal assignment record).
- Date: Not in provided documents: memo date. The draft agreement is dated Sept 22, 2026 [D2, header].

**Request**

Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. asked to increase its facility with Meridian Trust Bank to $18.0 million [D5, ¶4]. The proposed facility is $18.0M: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver [D1, §3 note]. The draft agreement provides a Term Loan of $12,000,000 and a Revolving Commitment not to exceed $6,000,000 [D2, §2.1(a), §2.1(b)].

The existing facility is $12.0M: a $7.0M term loan and a $5.0M revolver, approved June 2023 [D5, ¶2]. The relationship notes record the request as made by Erik and Anders Halvorsen on the 2026-08-19 call [D5, ¶4].

**Terms**

The Term Loan matures five years after the Closing Date and amortizes on a seven-year schedule, with the unpaid principal balance due at maturity [D2, §2.1(a)]. The Revolving Commitment and all revolving loans are due five years after the Closing Date [D2, §2.1(b)].

The obligations are secured by a first-priority security interest in all present and future assets, a first mortgage on the Rockford, Illinois plant, and a limited guaranty from Erik Halvorsen capped at $3,000,000 in the aggregate [D2, §2.2].

**Purpose and use of proceeds**

Term Loan and revolving loan proceeds are limited to refinancing the existing term loan owed to the Lender, funding the Expansion Project, and paying fees and expenses [D2, §2.1(c)]. Term loan proceeds: refinance the existing Meridian term loan (5,600), fund the plant expansion (6,000), and pay fees (400), for a total of 12,000 [D1, §3 note].

The borrower describes a 60,000 sq ft expansion of the Rockford plant ($6.0 million) tied to a new multi-year Customer A program [D5, ¶4]. Management expects added capacity for that program beginning in 2027 [D1, §6].

**Pro forma position (FY2025 basis)**

Pro forma total funded debt is 26,200: proposed term loan 12,000, Meridian revolver 3,200 and equipment notes 11,000 [D1, §3 note]. Pro forma total leverage is 2.52x [D1, §3]. Pro forma debt service is 5,600 and pro forma DSCR is 1.38x [D1, §3].

**Timing**

The borrower wants to close by November 30, 2026, so construction can start before winter [D5, ¶4]. The borrower states that a national bank has offered to deliver a term sheet within 10 business days [D5, ¶4].

**Sources used:** D1 §3 (Table 3 and note), §6; D2 header, §2.1(a)-(c), §2.2; D5 ¶2, ¶4.

**Underwriter to complete:**
- Header fields: request type, underwriter, senior reviewer and memo date (not in provided documents).
- New-money status: D4 §4.2.3 applies to "new-money" requests [D4, §4.2.3]. The provided documents do not state whether this request is classified as new-money. The underwriter should determine this and any resulting senior review requirement.
- Expansion Project: the term has the meaning given in Schedule 1.1, which is not in the excerpt [D2, §1.1]. Not in provided documents: the Schedule 1.1 definition.
- Revolver purpose: the documents do not state the intended use of the revolver beyond D2 §2.1(c). Not in provided documents: the revolver draw plan (borrower request letter or term sheet).
- Competing offer: the national bank offer is recorded only as the borrower's statement [D5, ¶4]. No term sheet is in the provided documents.
- Policy items for Section 6: the pro forma figures above are relevant to D4 §4.2.1-§4.2.3, and the underwriter applies those tests.
- Source discrepancy for Section 3: the Management commentary states net income of "$4.2 million" for FY2025 [D1, §6], while Table 1 shows net income of 3,900 for FY2025 [D1, §1: Net income, FY2025]. CONFLICT. I have not chosen between them.

sections.title: Borrower Overview and Relationship History
sections.author: M
sections.text:
D3 Part A defines no Section 2 subsections. Headings follow the D3 Part B exemplar.

**Company Profile**

Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. is privately held. [D5, ¶1] It was founded in 1994 in Rockford, Illinois, by Erik and Maria Halvorsen. [D5, ¶1]

The company makes precision-machined components and welded assemblies for agricultural and construction equipment OEMs. [D5, ¶1] It has about 310 employees and one plant. [D5, ¶1]

**Ownership and Management**

Ownership is Erik Halvorsen 55%, Maria Halvorsen 25%, and Anders Halvorsen (COO) 20%. [D5, ¶1] The draft credit agreement defines "Founders" as Erik Halvorsen and Maria Halvorsen. [D2, §1.1]

**Relationship History**

Larkspur has been a deposit and treasury management customer of Meridian since 2019. [D5, ¶2] Average operating deposits were $4.1 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026. [D5, ¶2]

A $12.0 million facility ($7.0M term loan, $5.0M revolver) was approved in June 2023. [D5, ¶2] The facility was paid as agreed with no past dues. [D5, ¶2]

The Q4 2024 compliance certificate arrived 18 days late. [D5, ¶3] Credit Administration waived the reporting covenant (waiver W-25-0117). [D5, ¶3] All later certificates arrived on time. [D5, ¶3]

The FY2025 compliance certificate is dated April 28, 2026. [D1, §7]

**Recent Developments**

On the 2026-08-19 call, Erik and Anders Halvorsen asked to increase the facility to $18.0 million. [D5, ¶4] The increase would fund a 60,000 sq ft expansion of the Rockford plant ($6.0 million), tied to a new multi-year Customer A program. [D5, ¶4]

They want to close by November 30, 2026, so construction can start before winter. [D5, ¶4] They said a national bank has offered a term sheet within 10 business days. [D5, ¶4]

On the 2026-09-02 call, Erik Halvorsen (64) said he plans to hand the CEO role to Anders within three years. [D5, ¶5] The family has informally discussed selling a minority stake to a private equity firm. [D5, ¶5] There is no timeline and no LOI. [D5, ¶5]

**Sources used:** D1 §7; D2 §1.1; D5 ¶1, ¶2, ¶3, ¶4, ¶5. D3 Part B §2 was used only as a house-style reference. Its facts match D5 ¶1 and ¶2.

**Underwriter to complete:**
- **Change of control (§7.6):** D2 §7.6 makes it an Event of Default if the Founders cease to own "a meaningful portion of the voting equity interests" or cease to be "actively involved in the management of the Borrower." [D2, §7.6] The terms "meaningful portion" and "actively involved" are not defined in the excerpt. Refer them to the underwriter and legal. Whether the CEO transition or a minority stake sale in D5 ¶5 bears on these terms is for the underwriter and legal to determine.
- **Waiver W-25-0117:** D5 ¶3 refers only to "the reporting covenant." Not in provided documents: the waiver document and the existing 2023 credit agreement section it relates to; these would normally be held by Credit Administration or the loan file.
- **Not in provided documents:** the borrower's legal form and state of incorporation, and management biographies beyond the names and roles above. The corporate records or the full credit file would normally hold these.
- **Header fields:** Underwriter, Senior reviewer and Date are not in the provided documents.

sections.title: Financial Analysis
sections.author: M
sections.text:
FY2023-FY2025 were audited by Hartwell & Lo LLP with unqualified opinions. Figures are in $ thousands unless stated. [D1, header]

### 3.1 Revenue and Earnings

Revenue was 61,400 in FY2023, 66,800 in FY2024 and 72,500 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Revenue, FY2023-FY2025]

Revenue growth was 6.0% in FY2023, 8.8% in FY2024 and 8.5% in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Revenue growth, FY2023-FY2025]

EBITDA was 8,600 in FY2023, 9,500 in FY2024 and 10,400 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: EBITDA, FY2023-FY2025]

EBITDA margin was 14.0% in FY2023, 14.2% in FY2024 and 14.3% in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: EBITDA margin, FY2023-FY2025]

Net income was 3,100 in FY2023 and 3,600 in FY2024. [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2023-FY2024]

**CONFLICT** on FY2025 net income:
- The spread table shows 3,900. [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2025]
- The borrower's FY2025 letter, as summarized by the analyst, states "Net income rose to $4.2 million." [D1, §6]

This draft does not choose between the two values.

Management attributes FY2025 revenue growth to "new agricultural OEM programs" (analyst's summary of the borrower's letter). [D1, §6]

Management attributes the EBITDA margin movement to "cell automation installed in 2024" (analyst's summary of the borrower's letter). [D1, §6]

### 3.2 Leverage and Debt Service

Total funded debt was 22,400 in FY2023, 20,900 in FY2024 and 19,800 in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: Total funded debt, FY2023-FY2025]

Total leverage was 2.60x in FY2023, 2.20x in FY2024 and 1.90x in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: Total leverage, FY2023-FY2025]

DSCR was 1.42x in FY2023, 1.55x in FY2024 and 1.61x in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: DSCR, FY2023-FY2025]

Debt service (P+I) was 4,500 in FY2023, 4,550 in FY2024 and 4,800 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Debt service (P+I), FY2023-FY2025]

Unfunded capex was 1,200 in FY2023, 1,300 in FY2024 and 1,400 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Unfunded capex, FY2023-FY2025]

Cash taxes were 1,000 in FY2023, 1,150 in FY2024 and 1,250 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Cash taxes, FY2023-FY2025]

FY2025 total funded debt comprised the Meridian term loan 5,600, the Meridian revolver 3,200 and the Prairie Equipment Finance equipment notes 11,000. [D1, §4]

As spread, total leverage is total funded debt divided by EBITDA. DSCR is (EBITDA minus unfunded capex minus cash taxes) divided by debt service (P+I). [D1, §2: Definitions as spread]

The draft agreement defines the Total Leverage Ratio as Total Funded Debt (including the Equipment Notes) divided by EBITDA for the four consecutive fiscal quarters then ended. [D2, §1.1]

The draft agreement defines the Debt Service Coverage Ratio as EBITDA minus Unfinanced Capital Expenditures minus cash taxes paid, divided by scheduled payments of principal and interest on Total Funded Debt. [D2, §1.1]

### 3.3 Liquidity

Cash was 2,100 in FY2023 and 2,600 in FY2024. [D1, Table 2: Cash, FY2023-FY2024]

Revolver availability was 1,800 in FY2023, 2,300 in FY2024 and 1,800 in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: Revolver availability, FY2023-FY2025]

Liquidity (cash + availability) was 3,900 in FY2023 and 4,900 in FY2024. [D1, Table 2: Liquidity (cash + availability), FY2023-FY2024]

Not in provided documents: FY2025 year-end cash and FY2025 liquidity. The spread export omits them. Year-end bank statements, due with the Q3 2026 package, would normally show the cash balance. [D1, §2: Footnote *]

### 3.4 Pro Forma for Proposed Facility

The proposed facility is $18.0M in total: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver. [D1, §3: Note to Table 3]

Pro forma (FY2025 basis) total funded debt is 26,200. [D1, Table 3: Total funded debt, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]

Pro forma total leverage is 2.52x. [D1, Table 3: Total leverage, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]

Pro forma debt service is 5,600. [D1, Table 3: Debt service, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]

Pro forma DSCR is 1.38x. [D1, Table 3: DSCR, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]

Pro forma total funded debt of 26,200 comprises the proposed term loan 12,000, the Meridian revolver 3,200 and the equipment notes 11,000. [D1, §3: Note to Table 3]

Term loan proceeds of 12,000 refinance the existing Meridian term loan 5,600, fund the plant expansion 6,000 and pay fees 400. [D1, §3: Note to Table 3]

The draft agreement limits use of proceeds to refinancing the existing term loan owed to the Lender, funding the Expansion Project, and paying fees and expenses. [D2, §2.1(c)]

The "Expansion Project" is defined by reference to Schedule 1.1. Not in provided documents: the Schedule 1.1 definition. [D2, §1.1]

### 3.5 Underwriter Commentary [U]

Section 3.5 is underwriter-authored.

**Sources used:**
- D1: header; §2 (definitions and Footnote *); §3 (Note to Table 3); §4; §6; Tables 1, 2 and 3.
- D2: §1.1; §2.1(c).
- D3: Part A (section list and style rules).

**Underwriter to complete:**
1. **CONFLICT, FY2025 net income:** 3,900 [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2025] against "$4.2 million" [D1, §6]. Resolve against the audited statements.
2. **Missing FY2025 data:** year-end cash and liquidity are not in the documents. The source is the year-end bank statements due with the Q3 2026 package [D1, §2: Footnote *].
3. **Definition differences for review:**
   - The spread DSCR uses "unfunded capex" and "debt service (P+I)" [D1, §2]. The draft agreement uses "Unfinanced Capital Expenditures" and "scheduled payments of principal and interest on Total Funded Debt" [D2, §1.1]. The spread ratios may not be on the agreement basis. Confirm whether they are comparable.
   - The spread does not state how EBITDA is built. The draft agreement defines EBITDA from GAAP net income [D2, §1.1]. Confirm the spread EBITDA matches.
4. **Pro forma basis:** the pro forma figures are on a FY2025 basis [D1, Table 3]. The pro forma revolver balance of 3,200 [D1, §3: Note to Table 3] sits within a $6.0M revolver commitment [D2, §2.1(b)]. Pro forma revolver availability is not stated in the documents.
5. **Policy items for Section 6 and the underwriter's judgment:**
   - Pro forma DSCR is 1.38x [D1, Table 3] against the policy minimum of 1.25x [D4, §4.2.2].
   - Pro forma total leverage is 2.52x [D1, Table 3] against the policy maximum of 3.50x [D4, §4.2.1].
   - Senior review is triggered where total commitment exceeds $15.0 million [D4, §4.2.3(a)]. The proposed commitment is $18.0M [D1, §3: Note to Table 3].
   - Customer A was 31% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5]. Policy requires concentration to be addressed in Section 7 when a single customer exceeds 25% [D4, §4.2.4].
6. **Section 3.5 Underwriter Commentary:** reserved for the underwriter.

### 4.1 Existing Covenants and Compliance (2023 Credit Agreement)

The FY2025 compliance certificate under the existing 2023 credit agreement is dated April 28, 2026 [D1, §7]. Total leverage was 1.90x against a 3.50x maximum [D1, §7]. DSCR was 1.61x against a 1.20x minimum [D1, §7]. The borrower complied with both financial covenants [D1, §7].

The 2023 facility had two financial covenants, each tested quarterly: a maximum total leverage ratio of 3.50x and a minimum DSCR of 1.20x [D3, Part B §4].

The Q4 2024 compliance certificate arrived 18 days late [D5, ¶3]. Credit Administration waived the reporting covenant under waiver W-25-0117 [D5, ¶3]. All later certificates arrived on time [D5, ¶3].

**Maximum Total Leverage Ratio.** "The Borrower shall not permit the Total Leverage Ratio, as of the last day of any fiscal quarter, to exceed 3.25 to 1.00; provided that for each fiscal quarter ending on or after December 31, 2027, the maximum shall be 3.00 to 1.00." [D2, §7.1] The ratio is Total Funded Debt on the test date divided by EBITDA for the four consecutive fiscal quarters then ended [D2, §1.1].

**Minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio.** "The Borrower shall not permit the Debt Service Coverage Ratio to be less than 1.25 to 1.00 as of the last day of any fiscal quarter." **Capital Expenditures.** "Unfinanced Capital Expenditures shall not exceed $2,500,000 in any fiscal year; provided that capital expenditures for the Expansion Project, not exceeding $6,000,000 in the aggregate, shall be excluded." [D2, §7.3] "Expansion Project" is defined in Schedule 1.1, which is not in the excerpt [D2, §1.1].

The Borrower must deliver the following [D2, §7.4]:
- Annual consolidated financial statements, audited by an independent accounting firm acceptable to the Lender, within 120 days after each fiscal year end [D2, §7.4(a)].

The covenant definitions, a covenant compliance calculation, or the full draft agreement would normally contain this.

  - The spread's ratios are on an annual FY2025 basis [D1, Table 3]. D2 tests quarterly on trailing four quarters [D2, §7.1, §7.2]. No quarterly pro forma is provided.

- **Event of Default provisions.** No other Events of Default (payment, cross-default, cure periods) appear in the excerpt. Not in provided documents: the full Events of Default article of the draft agreement.

sections.title: Policy Compliance and Exceptions
sections.author: M
sections.text:
**Policy basis**

The requested facility is subject to Meridian Commercial Credit Policy §4.2, Middle-Market Cash Flow Lending, v2026.1, effective March 1, 2026 [D4, §4.2]. Section 4.2 applies to new-money and renewal requests for middle-market borrowers underwritten on a cash flow basis [D4, §4.2].

**§4.2.1 Leverage**

Policy states that pro forma total leverage at origination shall not exceed 3.50x [D4, §4.2.1]. Any request above 3.50x is a policy exception and requires Chief Credit Officer approval [D4, §4.2.1]. Pro forma total leverage on an FY2025 basis is 2.52x [D1, Table 3: Total leverage, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)], on pro forma total funded debt of 26,200 [D1, Table 3: Total funded debt, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]. This is below 3.50x, and the figures indicate no leverage exception.

**§4.2.2 Debt service**

Policy states that pro forma DSCR at origination shall be at least 1.25x [D4, §4.2.2]. Any request below 1.25x is a policy exception [D4, §4.2.2]. Pro forma DSCR is 1.38x, on pro forma debt service of 5,600 [D1, Table 3: DSCR and Debt service, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]. This is above 1.25x, and the figures indicate no DSCR exception.

**§4.2.3 Senior review**

Policy requires senior underwriter review and Senior Loan Committee approval for any new-money request meeting any of three conditions [D4, §4.2.3].

- **(a) Total commitment above $15.0 million.** The proposed facility is $18.0M: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver [D1, §3 note]. The draft agreement states a Term Loan of $12,000,000 and a Revolving Commitment not to exceed $6,000,000 [D2, §2.1(a), §2.1(b)]. The $18.0M commitment exceeds $15.0 million, so condition (a) is met.
- **(b) Pro forma total leverage above 3.00x.** Pro forma total leverage is 2.52x [D1, Table 3: Total leverage, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]. Condition (b) is not met on the stated figure.
- **(c) Any policy exception present.** The figures above indicate no exception under §4.2.1 or §4.2.2 [D4, §4.2.1; D4, §4.2.2; D1, Table 3]. Condition (c) is not met on those figures.

**§4.2.4 Concentration**

Policy states that if any single customer exceeds 25% of borrower revenue in the most recent fiscal year, the credit memo must address customer concentration in Section 7, Key Risks and Mitigants [D4, §4.2.4]. Customer A accounted for 31% of FY2025 revenue and 28% of FY2024 revenue [D1, §5]. The top five customers accounted for 64% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5]. Customer A's 31% exceeds 25%, so the Section 7 requirement is triggered.

**§4.2.5 Risk rating**

Policy requires a risk rating on the bank's 1-10 scale with a written rationale in Section 9 [D4, §4.2.5]. The underwriter assigns the rating and the senior reviewer confirms it [D4, §4.2.5].

**Sources used:** D1 §3 note, §5, Table 3; D2 §2.1(a), §2.1(b); D4 §4.2, §4.2.1 to §4.2.5.

**Underwriter to complete:**

The requested facility is subject to Meridian Commercial Credit Policy §4.2, Middle-Market Cash Flow Lending, v2026.1, effective March 1, 2026 [D4, §4.2]. Section 4.2 applies to new-money and renewal requests for middle-market borrowers underwritten on a cash flow basis [D4, §4.2].

**§4.2.1 Leverage**

Policy states that pro forma total leverage at origination shall not exceed 3.50x [D4, §4.2.1]. Any request above 3.50x is a policy exception and requires Chief Credit Officer approval [D4, §4.2.1]. Pro forma total leverage on an FY2025 basis is 2.52x [D1, Table 3: Total leverage, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)], on pro forma total funded debt of 26,200 [D1, Table 3: Total funded debt, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]. This is below 3.50x, and the figures indicate no leverage exception.

**§4.2.2 Debt service**

Policy states that pro forma DSCR at origination shall be at least 1.25x [D4, §4.2.2]. Any request below 1.25x is a policy exception [D4, §4.2.2]. Pro forma DSCR is 1.38x, on pro forma debt service of 5,600 [D1, Table 3: DSCR and Debt service, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)]. This is above 1.25x, and the figures indicate no DSCR exception.

**§4.2.3 Senior review**

Policy requires senior underwriter review and Senior Loan Committee approval for any new-money request meeting any of three conditions [D4, §4.2.3].

Customer A accounted for 31% of FY2025 revenue and 28% of FY2024 revenue [D1, §5]. The top five customers accounted for 64% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5]. Customer A's 31% exceeds 25%, so the Section 7 requirement is triggered.

Policy requires a risk rating on the bank's 1-10 scale with a written rationale in Section 9 [D4, §4.2.5]. The underwriter assigns the rating and the senior reviewer confirms it [D4, §4.2.5].
